items.answer: Turn the two Watchlist repayment-delay indicators into Watchlist levels (WL). Indicator 2 (days with delay) and Indicator 3 (delays in 12 months) each get the list of options the later POC screens show, plus a pure function that maps the selected option to a WL. Success: for every option, the exported function returns the WL in the REQ table and C2, and any other input throws a RangeError (C1/C5). The full suite passes with `node --test`.
items.source: Request title + Requirements table (REQ-03-02, REQ-03-03), C1, C2, C4, C5, Contract

items.answer: No end user touches this slice directly. The consumers are the POC screens that other parts will build later and that import the modules (C4). This slice has no UI, roles, permissions or visibility rules.

items.answer: IN: REQ-03-02 -> src/indicators/daysWithDelay.mjs (DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS, daysWithDelayWl). REQ-03-03 -> src/indicators/delayCount.mjs (DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS, delayCountWl). Unit tests (dev) and contract/integration tests (QA) run by `node --test`. OUT: Indicator 1 (repayment delay yes/no) and its collapsing of indicators 2-3 (C3). Any UI or rendering of the dropdowns (C4). Counting the delays in the last 12 months (the caller does it, C6). All other EPIC-03 indicators and any aggregation of indicator WLs into an overall client WL ('Build only these two requirements'). No persistence and no I/O (CLAUDE.md).
items.source: Request header ('Build only these two requirements'), C3, C4, C6, Contract; repo CLAUDE.md

items.answer: Every option has a concrete expected value. daysWithDelayWl: 'no delay'->0, '<=3 days'->0, '>3 days'->2, '>60 days'->3, '>90 days'->4. delayCountWl: '0'->0, '1'->1, '>1'->2. Option lists in this order: DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS = ['no delay','<=3 days','>3 days','>60 days','>90 days'], DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS = ['0','1','>1']. Leading and trailing whitespace is accepted (' >3 days ' -> 2). These throw RangeError: case variants ('>3 Days'), unknown strings ('', '   ', '2', '<3 days', '≤3 days'), and non-strings (1, null, undefined, {}).
items.source: REQ-03-02 and REQ-03-03 acceptance column; C1, C2, C5; Contract

items.answer: Four apparent conflicts, each settled by the request itself. (1) The REQ-03-02 table writes '≤3 days', but C1 fixes the exact string as '<=3 days'. C1 wins, so '≤3 days' is an unknown value and throws RangeError. (2) The REQ acceptance column gives no WL for 'no delay', '≤3 days' or Indicator-3 '0'. C2 sets them to WL 0. (3) Read literally, '>60 days' and '>90 days' also satisfy '>3 days'. The dropdown is single-select and each option maps on its own, so '>60 days'->3 and '>90 days'->4, not 2. (4) Non-string input throws RangeError, not TypeError, as C5 explicitly states. No contradiction remains open.
items.source: REQ-03-02 vs C1; REQ-03-02/03 acceptance column vs C2; C5

items.answer: Both requirements are Must. They are independent and built in parallel, one developer each, so either one can merge on its own. There is no ordering dependency.

items.answer: ESM named exports. src/indicators/daysWithDelay.mjs exports const DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS (array of the 5 strings in C1 order) and function daysWithDelayWl(option: string): 0|2|3|4. src/indicators/delayCount.mjs exports const DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS (array of the 3 strings in C1 order) and function delayCountWl(option: string): 0|1|2. Return values are number primitives (WL 0-4, higher is worse). Both functions are synchronous and pure. The input is trimmed, then matched exactly and case-sensitively. null, undefined, numbers and other non-strings throw RangeError. Empty or whitespace-only input trims to '' and throws RangeError. See X-options-immutability, X-error-message and X-trim-semantics.
items.source: Contract; C1, C2, C5; repo CLAUDE.md

items.answer: Every invalid input throws a RangeError (instanceof RangeError), never returns a fallback WL and never returns undefined. Invalid means: a value not among the options after trimming, a wrong case, internal-whitespace variants such as '>3  days', an empty or whitespace-only string, a non-string (number 1, null, undefined, object, boolean, boxed new String('1')), and names inherited from Object.prototype such as 'constructor', 'toString' or '__proto__'. Message text: see X-error-message.
items.source: C1, C5
